clue.text: Hot stuff from Sun involved in slanderous attack

indicators.note: one thing involved in another is wrapped up inside it, so the star goes inside the mud

parts.note: slinging mud is making smearing, slanderous accusations
the Sun is a star

explanation.surface: A tabloid's spicy scoop arrives buried in a smear campaign against someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' and 'slanderous attack' suggest a tabloid newspaper, but no newspaper is involved: the Sun is just a heavenly body here.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustard is a pungent, fiery condiment, so it is hot stuff in the kitchen sense.

clue.text: Countless millions milk supplier put up

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means read from bottom to top, so the word for milk supplier runs backwards

parts.note: a dairy supplies milk

explanation.surface: Millions of pints from the dairy are stacked up, more than anyone can count.
explanation.definitionFit: Myriad as an adjective means innumerable, too many to number.

clue.text: Slow, losing heart and urge to change

indicators.note: a word losing its heart has its middle letters taken out, here from slow

parts.note: an itch is a restless urge or longing

explanation.surface: A sluggish person, now discouraged, feels the need for something different.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch is to swap one thing for another, a synonym of change.

clue.text: Organised sales base to include seconds subject to tax

indicators.note: to include means the shuffled letters contain the letter for seconds
organised means put into order, so the letters of sales base are rearranged

explanation.surface: A company's organised sales base takes in seconds, the slightly flawed goods, which the taxman notices.
explanation.definitionFit: Assessable income is liable to be assessed for taxation, so it is taxable.

clue.text: Detective exaggerated over the same thing

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters for exaggerated run backwards

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, meaning exaggerated

explanation.surface: A detective overstates the same point again.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is used to say that the same applies again, as in ditto marks.

clue.text: What an uninvited guest may do under it, possibly

definitions.text: What an uninvited guest may do

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of under it may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An uninvited guest might sneak in beneath something, perhaps a tent flap or a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who turns up unasked imposes on others, which is to intrude.

clue.text: New prison to include European court examiner

indicators.note: to include means the reworked letters take the other pieces into their middle
new means remade, so the letters of prison form a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A newly built jail incorporates a European court, an official checking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' anagrams PRISON to INSPOR, which wraps ECT.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is an official who examines premises or work to check standards.

clue.text: Movement bound to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard means the word is spoken, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: tied means bound, as with rope

explanation.surface: A political or social movement is certain to make itself heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to be heard' reads as 'certain to be heard'; 'bound' is TIED.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide is the regular rise and fall of the sea, a movement of water.

clue.text: Fix weapon held by American, protesting hotly

indicators.note: held by means kept inside, so the other pieces sit within the letters for American

parts.note: US is short for American, as in US forces
to pin is to fasten or fix in place
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: An American gets hold of a gun and protests angrily, a gun-rights row.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up in arms is an idiom for being angry and loudly objecting.

clue.text: Might this describe an orbit?

parts.note: orbit can mean the eye socket, and describe means to trace a line around, as cosmetics do

explanation.surface: It sounds like asking what traces a planet's path through space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orbit' suggests astronomy, but it is the anatomical eye socket; 'describe' is used in its geometric sense of drawing round.
explanation.definitionFit: This make-up is drawn as a line around the eyes, outlining the eye's socket.

clue.text: Helps to chase runs and attacks

indicators.note: to chase is to follow behind, so the word for helps comes after the abbreviation for runs

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
aids means helps, as a verb

explanation.surface: Assistance sets off after runners and launches assaults, like a battlefield report.
explanation.definitionFit: Raids are sudden assaults, so they are attacks in the plural noun sense.

clue.text: International campaign to evaluate vehicle

parts.note: a Test is an international match in cricket or rugby
a drive is an organised campaign, as in a recruitment drive

explanation.surface: An international campaign is launched to assess some vehicle, like a government safety programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To test-drive is to try out a car on the road before buying, assessing how it performs.

clue.text: Usual male in charge beginning to doubt

indicators.note: in places the word for male inside the verb meaning charge

parts.note: to accuse is to charge with an offence
a tom is a male animal, especially a cat

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the opening letter of the word doubt

explanation.surface: An ordinary man in a position of authority begins to have misgivings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In charge' looks like a phrase meaning responsible; split it so 'in' is the container signal and 'charge' a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Accustomed as an adjective means habitual or customary, as in his accustomed seat.

clue.text: Expedition dispensing with a fine outfit

indicators.note: dispensing with means doing without, so these letters are removed from the word for expedition

parts.note: a safari is an expedition, typically to view wildlife
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: A trip abandoning a fine outfit, as if packing light for the bush.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is a garment of draped cloth worn in South Asia, so it is an outfit.

clue.text: Surprised man on alert for decorative plant

indicators.note: someone surprised is thrown into confusion, so the letters of man on alert are scattered

explanation.surface: A startled man is on watch, guarding a decorative plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental is a plant grown for its looks rather than for food or use.

clue.text: You'd better believe that I don't want responsibility for technology

definitions.meaning: the phrase is an assurance that the speaker knows what they are talking about

definitions.text: I don't want responsibility for technology
definitions.meaning: read literally, take IT, information technology, away from me

explanation.surface: A frustrated worker insists they want nothing to do with the computers.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is the usual abbreviation for information technology, which makes the second reading a request to remove it from the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Take it from me is an idiom used to urge someone to trust what you say.

clue.text: Bringing about ten for a change and suffering

indicators.note: for a change means altered, so the letters of ten are rearranged

parts.note: ailing means unwell, suffering from illness

explanation.surface: Ten people, for once, are both causing something and in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve or cause as a consequence, so entailing is bringing about.

clue.text: Standing men only name worker

parts.note: a stag party or night is for men only
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A sign reads 'Standing: men only', and a name is given to the worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing' looks like position or status, but it is standing water.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water is still and unmoving, which is what standing water means.

clue.text: Needing money from son, in a corner

parts.note: someone in a corner is trapped with no escape

explanation.surface: A cornered parent gets a request for cash from their son.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped, short for strapped for cash, means short of funds.

clue.text: Reckon Italian song not initially oppressive

parts.note: to total is to add up or reckon a sum
an aria is a song in an opera

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word not

explanation.surface: Someone tots up an Italian song that, at first, isn't oppressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' looks like a negation of 'oppressive', but it just supplies N.
explanation.definitionFit: A totalitarian regime controls every aspect of life, so it is harshly oppressive.

clue.text: Juliet needs a minder, mostly for cat

parts.note: Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of the word for minder is dropped

parts.note: a guard is a minder or protector

explanation.surface: Juliet needs a bodyguard, probably to deal with a big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The jaguar is a large spotted wild feline of the Americas.

clue.text: Resolve to pay

definitions.meaning: to ... a dispute is to resolve it
to ... a bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: Someone makes a firm decision to hand over the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Settle covers both ending a disagreement and clearing a debt.

clue.text: Attack fully-grown kid

definitions.meaning: a kid is a young ..., so a kid fully grown is the adult animal

explanation.surface: An adult child is told to go on the offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is the young of a goat.
explanation.definitionFit: Go at is an idiom for attack, and a kid grows into this farm animal.

clue.text: Handle that may be used only occasionally?

definitions.text: Handle that may be used only occasionally?

parts.words: Handle that may be used only occasionally?
parts.note: handle is slang for a person's name, and the one between first name and surname is seldom spoken

explanation.surface: A door handle or tool that hardly ever gets used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' suggests something you grip; it is slang for a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The extra given name between first name and surname is rarely used in everyday address.

clue.text: Steer clear of daughter held by magistrate

indicators.note: held by means kept within, so the letter for daughter goes inside the word for magistrate

parts.note: the Doge was the chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa

explanation.surface: Someone avoids their daughter, who has been detained by a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge something is to avoid it by moving aside, which is to steer clear.

clue.text: Part of problem in ironing dress

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A snag while pressing clothes leaves a dress damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A mini is a very short skirt or dress, short for minidress.

clue.text: A politician prevaricated about one female and added more detail

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for prevaricated goes round the other letters

parts.note: to prevaricate is to evade the truth, close to lied
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An MP fibbed about a woman and then embellished the story further.
explanation.definitionFit: To amplify a statement is to expand on it, filling in further particulars.

clue.text: Mock turtle's first relation

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word turtle's

parts.note: an aunt is a family relation

explanation.surface: It evokes the Mock Turtle of Alice in Wonderland and its first relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock turtle' reads as Lewis Carroll's character, but 'Mock' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To taunt someone is to jeer at or ridicule them, which is to mock.

clue.text: Lost dignity doing some work around house

indicators.note: lost dignity has gone astray, so its letters wander into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone forfeits their self-respect by doing chores at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidying is putting things in order, a routine household chore.

clue.text: Poor angler has right of course to elaborate

indicators.note: a poor angler is a bad one, so the letters of angler are badly arranged
the right of a written word is its end, so this takes the final letter of course

explanation.surface: An unsuccessful fisherman has fishing rights on a stretch of river and boasts about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right of course' looks like a fishing right, but it is the last letter of 'course'.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge on a subject is to expand on it in detail, which is to elaborate.
